name: Question 15
problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+{e}^{-t}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system is

| $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+$ {{field-1}} $\cdot \,\,$ |  | $-\frac{7}{10}$ |  |

|  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
{e}^{-t}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is exponential. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also exponential, i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)={e}^{-t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}],
$$

where $a,b$  are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the derivative of ${x}_{p}$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{x}_{p}^{′}(t)=-{e}^{-t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the unknown constants, we substitute ${x}_{p}$ and ${x}_{p}^{′}$ into our system:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{e}^{-t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot {e}^{-t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]+{e}^{-t}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ -[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-a \\ -b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3b \\ 3a\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-a \\ -b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3b+4 \\ 3a+1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3b+4=-a \\ 3a+1=-b\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we get 

$$
a=3b-4.
$$

 
Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $b,$ we have

$$
3(3b-4)+1=-b\,⇒\,b=\frac{11}{10}.
$$

So, 

$$
a=3\cdot \frac{11}{10}-4=\frac{33}{10}-\frac{40}{10}=-\frac{7}{10}.
$$

 

Therefore, the particular solution is

$$
{x}_{p}(t)={e}^{-t}[\begin{aligned}-\frac{7}{10} \\ \frac{11}{10}\end{aligned}].
$$
